question: Lack of transparency surrounding the removal of the EUR 80 million ‘Trust your Stars’ project from Greece’s Recovery and Resilience Plan – risk of a permanent brain drain

According to a report by Politico1, hundreds of Greek and European scientists have been confronted with professional uncertainty following the sudden and non-transparent decision to remove the EUR 80 million ‘Trust your Stars’ research programme from the revised Greek Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF) plan.

The programme, which had been strategically designed and approved, had aimed at bringing highly qualified scientists back to Greece (an initiative dubbed ‘brain regain’). Instead, however, distinguished researchers who have resigned from positions abroad on the basis of official government assurances have found themselves left in the lurch.

The corresponding EU funding has been redirected by the Greek Government, without any transparency or public accountability, exacerbating the major problem that is the country’s demographic survival2,3,4,5. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
Is the Commission fully aware of the exact reasons why the Greek Government removed RRF funding from such a vital project aimed at addressing the brain drain?
What control mechanisms will it put in place to ensure that RRF funds that have been approved to support Member States’ demographic and social cohesion are not removed or arbitrarily redirected?
What EU safeguards are in place to protect researchers with professional commitments to RRF-funded programmes and to ensure that they do not become victims of national mismanagement?
